historical_claims.anchor: In specialized root-cap cells, relatively dense, starch-filled structures called statoliths settle in response to gravity.
In roots, a higher auxin signal on the lower flank can inhibit elongation there, so the other side grows faster and the root bends downward.
Sugars produced by photosynthesis travel through another tissue, phloem, from sources such as mature leaves toward sinks such as growing roots, developing fruits, seeds, or storage organs.
Under water shortage, the hormone abscisic acid participates in a signaling network that promotes closure.
When two action potentials occur close enough together, the trap can close rapidly.
The number and timing of signals matter to different stages of the response.
In controlled experiments, plants exposed to volatile chemicals from damaged neighbors can alter their own defense-related signaling and become more responsive when attacked later.

In the model plant Arabidopsis, the timing of activity of a regulator called CONSTANS and the stability of its protein help determine whether a leaf activates a flowering signal called FLOWERING LOCUS T.

description: Examines plant water and sugar transport, light and gravity responses, hormones, electric signals, defense, and seasonal timing.
